title: "1. How accurately do the models pose the effector?"

Scored on `ra_eff`, the receptor-aligned effector RMSD, with < 5 Å counting as
correctly posed. Each variant contributes one prediction per target. That is its
own most confident of 25 (5 seeds x 5 diffusion samples), selected on mean pLDDT
without reference to the answer.

```{python}
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "../../bin")
from _analysis_common import *

d = load()
df, combos = d["df"], d["combos"]
```

## Accuracy per model

```{python}
xs, n_no = block_positions(combos)
series = {c: df[(df["msa"] == c[0]) & (df["model"] == c[1])][RA_COL].values
          for c in combos}

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(max(11, 0.75 * len(combos) + 3), 6.4))
bp = ax.boxplot([series[c] for c in combos], positions=xs, widths=0.6,
                patch_artist=True, showfliers=False,
                medianprops=dict(color="black"))

rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
for patch, x, (flag, model) in zip(bp["boxes"], xs, combos):
    patch.set_facecolor(NO_MSA_COLOR if flag == "no_msa" else MSA_COLOR)
    patch.set_alpha(0.55)
    if is_oracle(model):
        patch.set_hatch("///")
        patch.set_edgecolor("black")
    y = series[(flag, model)]
    ax.scatter(x + rng.uniform(-0.15, 0.15, len(y)), y, s=14, color="black",
               alpha=0.45, zorder=3)

ax.axhline(RA_EFF_THRESHOLD, ls="--", color="grey", lw=1)
ax.axvline(n_no, color="lightgrey", lw=1)
ax.set_yscale("log")
readable_log(ax.yaxis, RA_TICKS)
ax.set_ylabel("Receptor-aligned effector RMSD (Å, log scale)")
ax.set_xticks(xs)
ax.set_xticklabels([pretty(m) for _, m in combos], rotation=45, ha="right",
                   fontsize=9)

top = ax.get_ylim()[1]
for x, c in zip(xs, combos):
    ax.text(x, top * 1.15, f"{int((series[c] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD).sum())}/{len(series[c])}",
            ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylim(ax.get_ylim()[0], top * 1.8)

handles = [plt.Rectangle((0, 0), 1, 1, fc=c, alpha=0.55, ec="black")
           for c in (NO_MSA_COLOR, MSA_COLOR)]
handles.append(plt.Rectangle((0, 0), 1, 1, fc="white", ec="black", hatch="///"))
ax.legend(handles, ["No MSA", "MSA", "restraints from\nthe reference"],
          loc="center left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 0.5), frameon=True, fontsize=9)
save_fig(fig, "pose_accuracy_by_model", thesis=True)
plt.show()

pd.DataFrame([
    {"model": DISPLAY.get(m, m), "msa": MSA_LABEL[f], "n": len(series[(f, m)]),
     "median ra_eff": round(float(np.median(series[(f, m)])), 2),
     "n correct": int((series[(f, m)] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD).sum()),
     "% correct": round(100 * (series[(f, m)] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD).mean(), 1)}
    for f, m in combos]).sort_values("median ra_eff").reset_index(drop=True)
```

- The MSA setting is the largest single driver of accuracy. The MSA block sits
  well below the no-MSA block on both median and count.
- The hatched variants are not predictors. Their restraints are derived from the
  reference complex, so they cannot be run on a novel target. They measure how
  far a model can be driven towards an interface it is told about, and should be
  read as a positive control rather than part of the ranking.
- Boltz-2 responds to correct restraints far more than Boltz-1 does, which is
  why it is the model negative steering is built on.
- Pairs of references encoding the same complex disagree by a wide margin on
  this benchmark, so small differences between variants are not differences in
  capability.

## Which targets are hard?

```{python}
per_pdb = (df.assign(ok=df[RA_COL] < RA_EFF_THRESHOLD)
             .groupby(["system", "pdb"])["ok"].sum().astype(int).reset_index())

# Pik and RGA5 as separate blocks, each ordered easiest first.
xs, heights, labels, colours, bounds, cursor = [], [], [], [], [], 0.0
for system in ["Pik", "RGA5"]:
    blk = per_pdb[per_pdb["system"] == system].sort_values("ok", ascending=False)
    start = cursor
    for _, r in blk.iterrows():
        xs.append(cursor); heights.append(int(r["ok"])); labels.append(r["pdb"])
        colours.append(SYS_COLORS[system]); cursor += 1
    bounds.append((system, start, cursor - 1)); cursor += 1.2

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(max(10, 0.55 * len(xs) + 3), 6))
ax.bar(xs, heights, width=0.85, color=colours, edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.8)
for x, h in zip(xs, heights):
    ax.text(x, h + 0.15, str(h), ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=8)

band_lo, band_hi = len(combos) + 0.9, len(combos) + 2.0
for system, xa, xb in bounds:
    ax.add_patch(plt.Rectangle((xa - 0.46, band_lo), (xb - xa) + 0.92,
                               band_hi - band_lo, facecolor=SYS_COLORS[system],
                               alpha=0.30, edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.8))
    ax.text((xa + xb) / 2, (band_lo + band_hi) / 2, system, ha="center",
            va="center", fontsize=11, fontweight="bold")
ax.set_xticks(xs)
ax.set_xticklabels(labels, rotation=45, ha="right", fontsize=9)
ax.set_ylabel(f"Variants with receptor-aligned effector\nRMSD < {RA_EFF_THRESHOLD:g} Å")
ax.set_ylim(0, band_hi + 0.4)
save_fig(fig, "per_target_difficulty")
plt.show()

per_pdb.groupby("system")["ok"].agg(["count", "mean", "median", "min", "max"]).round(1)
```

- No target is solved by every variant, and difficulty is far from uniform.
- RGA5 is markedly harder than Pik, so the aggregate medians above are carried
  by the Pik targets.
- The benchmark set is homogeneous by construction, being 18 HMA/MAX-effector
  complexes from two NLR families, so none of this generalises to NLR-effector
  prediction at large.
